newsitem.title: USA: Sears begins $7/shr offer for MaxServ.
newsitem.headline: Sears begins $7/shr offer for MaxServ.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Tuesday it had begun a $7-a-share cash tender offer for all common shares of MaxServ Inc it does not already own.
Sears owned about 64.4 percent of MaxServ shares as of November 30, 1996.

Sears said it and members of a special committee of the MaxServ board of directors had previously sought to negotiate an offer. However, these negotiations have been unsuccessful to date and Sears' proposal to offer $7 in cash was rejected by the special committee, Sears said in a statement.
Sears Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Alan Lacy sent a letter to MaxServ's board advising it that Sears had begun the tender offer.
Sears told MaxServ directors that it believes the offer is fair to all stockholders (other than Sears).
Sears said the tender was driven by rejection of the offer and its inability to resolve differences over the value of the shares held by minority shareholders.
Sears also noted that investment bank Merrill Lynch & Co said the price was fair from a financial point of view.
Sears said its tender is not conditioned on any minimum number or shares being received or upon the approval of the directors of MaxServ or any committee of the MaxServ board.
Following completion of the tender offer, Sears said it intends to acquire any remaining MaxServ shares in a cash merger at the same price it paid in the tender.
Texas-based MaxServ provides information regarding the care, repair and usage of household products and other electronic products. It also provides telemarketing services for replacemnt parts.
MaxServ officials were not immediately available to comment on or respond to the offer.
Sears owns and operates more than 2,300 department and specialty stores in the the United States.
Shares of MaxServ were trading at 7-1/4, up 1/4.
